answer:
Group consecutive query heads around each shared KV head. Keeping a separate group axis lets batched matmul broadcast K/V without making a repeated KV tensor. Hkv=1 is MQA; Hkv=Hq is MHA. KV-cache storage scales with Hkv, but the number of query attention distributions still scales with Hq. repeat_interleave creates repeated values; it does not by itself avoid the memory copy. The reference still materializes scores and is not a fused GPU implementation.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** KV storage is $2BLSH_{kv}d_hb$ bytes for batch $B$, layers $L$, sequence length $S$, and $b$ bytes per element. Reducing KV heads from $H_q$ to $H_{kv}$ reduces that storage in the same ratio. Query heads remain distinct, so sharing KV heads does not collapse all heads to one attention distribution. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://aiexpjourney.substack.com/p/grouped-query-attention-gqa-explained-5f3dbbfe013b) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention.html).
